skill.name: writing-great-skills
skill.description: Reference for writing and editing AI skills with predictable invocation, clear information hierarchy, and maintainable wording.
skill.summary: Helps authors write predictable, maintainable AI skills.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: AI skills can become long, vague, and hard to invoke. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code authors vocabulary for predictable, maintainable skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains model-invoked and user-invoked skill tradeoffs.
Defines context load and cognitive load for invocation decisions.
Guides description pruning with branches, leading words, and relevance checks.
Shows when to disclose reference into linked files.
Lists failure modes such as premature completion, duplication, sediment, sprawl, and no-ops.
limitations: It is a reference, not a step-by-step scaffold generator.
It does not validate marketplace manifests or JSON schemas.
It does not include executable scripts, tests, or automation.
It assumes the reader is editing AI skill files.

use_cases.title: Refine Skill Descriptions
use_cases.description: Improve invocation text so agents trigger the right skill at the right time.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Decide what belongs in SKILL.md and what belongs in linked reference files.

use_cases.title: Audit Skill Prose
use_cases.description: Find duplication, stale content, and no-op instructions before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-great-skills to review this skill draft. Identify unclear invocation wording, duplicated ideas, and no-op sentences.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Invocation
prompt_templates.scenario: Make a model-invoked skill easier to trigger.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-great-skills to rewrite this skill description. Preserve the intent, reduce context load, and keep only distinct trigger branches.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Disclosure
prompt_templates.scenario: Decide what should move into reference files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-great-skills to map this skill onto the information hierarchy. Recommend which material should stay inline and which should move behind pointers.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign Skill Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-great-skills to evaluate whether these related skills should merge, split by invocation, split by sequence, or share external reference.

output_examples.input: Review a skill with a long description and repeated trigger phrases.
output: Collapse repeated trigger phrases into one branch.
Move background explanations from the description into the body.
Keep only wording that changes when the agent invokes the skill.

output_examples.input: Decide whether a glossary belongs inside SKILL.md.
output: Keep definitions inline when every run needs them.
Move specialized terms into a linked reference when only some branches need them.
Strengthen pointer wording before moving required material out of view.

output_examples.input: Find failure modes in a mature skill.
output: Check for premature completion where later steps distract from the current step.
Remove sediment that no longer affects behavior.
Replace weak leading words with terms that better anchor the intended behavior.

best_practices: Use the skill when deciding whether material belongs in SKILL.md or linked reference.
Keep one source of truth for each behavior and prune no-op prose.
Test invocation wording against real prompts before splitting a skill.
anti_patterns: Treating every helpful note as a required step.
Repeating the same meaning across description, body, and glossary.
Splitting skills before a clear invocation or sequence problem exists.

faq.question: What does this skill help me write?
faq.answer: It helps you write AI skills that are easier to invoke, maintain, and review.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete skill scaffold?
faq.answer: No. It provides principles and vocabulary for improving skill content and structure.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude and Codex skills?
faq.answer: Yes. The concepts apply to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill authoring.

faq.question: When should I use linked reference files?
faq.answer: Use them when material is useful only for some branches or would obscure primary steps.

faq.question: How does it improve skill descriptions?
faq.answer: It helps remove duplicate triggers and keep only wording that improves invocation.

faq.question: Does it include security checks?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on writing quality, invocation, structure, and maintainability.
